subject: History
description: Covers Brahmo Samaj and Satyashodhak Samaj.

questions.stem: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj, one of the most influential socio-religious reform movements in 19th-century India?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 in Calcutta. He was a pioneer of the Indian Renaissance. The Samaj campaigned tirelessly against the rigid caste system, polytheism, idol worship, and most famously, the brutal practice of Sati (which was successfully abolished by Lord William Bentinck in 1829 directly due to Roy's lobbying).
DECOY BUSTING: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897). Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj (1875). Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar championed widow remarriage.
EXAM INSIGHT: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was deeply influenced by Western modernism and Christianity, advocating for English education and scientific thinking in India.

questions.stem: Which 19th-century social reformer famously started the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' (Truth Seekers' Society) to secure human rights and social justice for low-caste people in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune in 1873. Its primary goal was to liberate the Shudras and Ati Shudras (untouchables) from the exploitation and oppression of Brahmins. He also fiercely advocated for women's education, opening the first native school for girls in Pune alongside his wife, Savitribai Phule.
DECOY BUSTING: Dr. Ambedkar led the Dalit Buddhist movement later in the 20th century. Periyar led the Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu. Narayan Guru led the reform movement in Kerala (SNDP Yogam).
EXAM INSIGHT: Phule's most famous book is 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery), published in 1873, which he dedicated to the anti-slavery movement in America.
